content.title: Algorithm for the treatment of patients with advanced heart failure
content.summary: Flowchart guiding management of advanced heart failure based on INTERMACS profile, use of short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS), assessment of neurological and end-organ recovery, evaluation of contraindications to heart transplantation (HT), consideration of LVAD as bridge-to-candidacy (LVAD-BTC) or destination therapy (LVAD-DT), and pathways for withdrawal, weaning, listing for HT or deferred advanced HF therapies.
key_nodes: INTERMACS levels (1, 2, 3-4, >4 'Stable ambulatory') guide initial pathway
Short-term MCS (BTD/BTR/BTB/BTT) indicated (Class IIa) for certain INTERMACS profiles
Assessment branches: persistence of severe brain damage/irreversible end-organ damage; cardiac, neurological and end-organ recovered; neurological and end-organ recovered but no cardiac recovery
If contraindications to HT present — determine whether potentially reversible; if reversible consider LVAD-BTC (Class IIa)
If contraindications reversed — consider listing for HT or de-listing with close follow-up if meaningful improvement (Class I)
If high surgical/HT risk or contraindications persist — consider advanced HF therapies or LVAD-DT (Class IIa), or withdrawal/weaning of MCS support

classes_and_colours.Class I: Green (for list for HT or de-listing with very close follow-up in case of meaningful improvement)
classes_and_colours.Class IIa: Yellow (short-term MCS, LVAD-BTC, LVAD-DT are shown as Class IIa in algorithm)

abbreviations_extracted.INTERMACS: Interagency Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support
abbreviations_extracted.ESC/HFA: European Society of Cardiology / Heart Failure Association

content.applicability_and_exceptions: Algorithm applies to all patients with advanced heart failure defined according to ESC/HFA criteria, with exceptions including HCM, CA, arrhythmic storm, adult congenital heart disease, and refractory angina.
content.prognostic_notes: Despite many prognostic parameters, predicting outcomes remains difficult; early referral to advanced HF centres may allow MCS and HT before end-organ damage develops.
content.selection_criteria_examples: Examples of criteria cited include recurrent hospitalization, progressive end-organ failure, refractory congestion, inability to perform cardiopulmonary exercise test or peak VO2 <12 mL/min/kg or <50% of expected value.
